visual: Bushy evergreen Mediterranean shrub with white woolly young stems, small aromatic dark green leaves with silvery-white undersides, and attractive pale blue flowers in summer.
water: Water regularly during establishment, then sparingly. Established plants tolerate relatively dry conditions well.
aspect: Full sun; sheltered south- or west-facing position
soil: Well-drained chalk, loam or sandy soil; neutral to alkaline conditions preferred.
soilWarning: Requires excellent drainage and shelter in the UK. Avoid heavy, persistently wet ground, particularly during winter.
prune: Prune in spring to maintain a compact shape, cutting back the previous year's growth while avoiding cutting unnecessarily into old bare wood.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten. Wear gloves and protective equipment when handling.
hardinessNote: Hardy in coastal and relatively mild parts of the UK, approximately -5 to 1°C. In colder areas grow against a warm sheltered wall or provide winter protection.
resilience: Drought tolerant and generally pest- and disease-free once established, but vulnerable to cold and winter wet.
uses: Mediterranean gardens, coastal planting, sunny borders, courtyard gardens and warm wall-side planting.
foliage: Evergreen; small aromatic dark green leaves with conspicuously silvery-white undersides.
container: Well suited to a large free-draining container, which can provide useful winter protection in colder locations.

visual: Clump-forming deciduous perennial grown for striking large heart-shaped silver leaves intricately edged and veined in green. Airy sprays of small vivid blue forget-me-not-like flowers rise above the foliage in spring.
water: Keep consistently moist during establishment and dry periods. Established plants tolerate some dry shade but perform best where the soil does not become excessively dry.
soil: Moderately fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sandy soil; tolerant of acid, neutral or alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged soil. Strong direct sun, particularly combined with dry soil, can scorch the silver foliage.
prune: No routine pruning required. Remove damaged or tired foliage and spent flower stems if desired.
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe, approximately -20 to -15°C.
resilience: Very hardy, low-maintenance and generally pest- and disease-free. An excellent shade perennial once established.
uses: Shade borders, woodland gardens, ground cover, banks, slopes and underplanting shrubs and roses.
foliage: Deciduous; large heart-shaped leaves are predominantly silver with contrasting green veins and margins.
container: Excellent in containers positioned in cool partial shade or shade, particularly for displaying the ornamental foliage.

visual: Rounded deciduous shrub with distinctive horizontal branching, strongly veined mid-green leaves and dense rounded clusters of pure white snowball-like flowers. Foliage develops red and purple autumn colour.
water: Water regularly while establishing. Once established, maintain moderate moisture during prolonged dry periods.
soil: Moderately fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; tolerant of acid, neutral or alkaline conditions.
prune: Pruning is normally minimal. Remove damaged, crossing or unwanted branches after flowering; tolerates renovation pruning if required.
toxicity: Ornamental fruits should not be eaten. Wear gloves when handling.
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe, approximately -20 to -15°C.
resilience: Very hardy and adaptable once established.
uses: Specimen shrub, mixed borders, cottage gardens, spring-flowering displays and autumn colour.
foliage: Deciduous; strongly veined mid-green leaves turning red and purple in autumn.
container: Possible while young but ultimately better planted in the ground.

visual: Compact variegated shrub with silvery-white and green foliage. New leaves are flushed pink and colour again in autumn and winter. Fragrant white to pale pink flowers are produced over a very long season.
water: Water regularly during establishment; relatively drought tolerant once established.
aspect: Full sun; sheltered south- or west-facing position preferred.
soil: Fertile, well-drained chalk, loam or sandy soil; tolerant of acid, neutral or alkaline pH.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged soil and cold exposed positions.
prune: Lightly prune after flowering to maintain shape. Older plants can receive harder renovation pruning every three to four years.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most UK locations, approximately -15 to -10°C, but benefits from shelter in colder areas.
resilience: Drought resistant once established but less suited to cold exposed sites.
uses: Sunny borders, patio containers, courtyard gardens, low hedging and wall-side planting.
foliage: Semi-evergreen; green leaves broadly variegated silvery white with seasonal pink flushing.
container: Excellent compact shrub for containers in a sunny sheltered position.
uncertain: RHS currently lists the cultivar name status as unresolved and gives Linnaea × grandiflora 'Sparkling Silver' as a synonym.

visual: Upright to spreading evergreen shrub with dark green foliage and fewer thorns than many traditional firethorns. White flower clusters in late spring are followed by masses of vivid red berries in autumn.
water: Water during establishment; established plants tolerate relatively dry conditions.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained or well-drained soil; tolerant of chalk, clay, loam and sand and a broad pH range.
prune: Flowers form mainly on previous year's growth. After flowering remove unwanted shoots and, on mature plants, selectively remove around one fifth of older wood while retaining fruiting growth.
toxicity: Ornamental fruits should not be eaten. Thorny growth can injure skin; wear gloves when handling.
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe, approximately -20 to -15°C.
resilience: Hardy, adaptable and tolerant of dry free-draining soils once established.
uses: Wildlife gardens, hedging, screens, wall training, security planting and autumn berry displays.
foliage: Evergreen; dark green leaves retained year-round.
container: Can be grown in a large container when young but performs best in the ground long term.
uncertain: The label's PBR notation was retained conceptually, but the RHS plant profile lists the plant simply as Pyracantha 'Red Star'.

visual: Vigorous medium-sized, semi-evergreen subshrub with greyish hairy stems and foliage, carrying abundant large light pink mallow-like flowers throughout summer.
water: Water during establishment and prolonged drought, but avoid excessive moisture.
soil: Well-drained chalk, loam or sandy soil; tolerant of acid, neutral and alkaline pH.
soilWarning: Good drainage is important, particularly over winter.
prune: Prune hard in spring to a low permanent framework, removing weak, damaged and dead growth.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most UK locations, approximately -15 to -10°C; shelter from severe cold winds is beneficial.
resilience: Fast-growing and floriferous but shrubby mallows can be relatively short-lived.
uses: Sunny borders, cottage gardens, pollinator planting and rapid summer flowering displays.
foliage: Semi-evergreen; hairy grey-green leaves on greyish stems.
container: Possible in a very large container, though generally better suited to open ground.
uncertain: Often still sold as Lavatera 'Rosea', Lavatera × clementii 'Rosea' or Lavatera olbia 'Rosea'; RHS currently accepts Malva × clementii 'Rosea'.

visual: Compact dense evergreen shrub with unusually bright silvery-grey, softly hairy oval leaves. Clusters of rich yellow daisy-like flowers appear above the silver foliage in summer.
water: Water during establishment, then moderately; tolerates relatively dry conditions once established.
soil: Well-drained soil in a sunny position; adaptable to chalk, clay, loam or sand where drainage is adequate.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently wet or waterlogged soil, especially during winter.
prune: Lightly prune after flowering to maintain a compact bushy shape and remove unwanted growth.
hardinessNote: Hardy through most of the UK, approximately -10 to -5°C; shelter is beneficial in colder districts.
resilience: Evergreen, drought tolerant once established and particularly useful for sunny, free-draining sites.
uses: Sunny borders, coastal planting, gravel gardens, Mediterranean-style planting, containers and silver-foliage schemes.
foliage: Evergreen; dense oval leaves covered with silvery-grey hairs.
container: Well suited to containers provided drainage is excellent.
uncertain: Frequently labelled Senecio 'Silver Dormouse'. Accepted trade presentation is Brachyglottis Walberton's Silver Dormouse ('Walbrach').

visual: Vigorous twining deciduous climber grown primarily for spectacular foliage. Mature leaves develop silver-white tips which later flush vivid pink, accompanied by small white flowers.
water: Maintain regular moisture during establishment and dry weather; prefers consistent moisture without waterlogging.
aspect: Full sun in a sheltered position
soil: Fertile, moist but well-drained soil; tolerant of chalk, clay, loam and sand and a broad pH range.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged soil. Too much shade substantially reduces the characteristic white and pink foliage colour.
prune: Prune established climbers in late winter, removing congested or unwanted growth and training remaining stems onto supports.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most UK locations, approximately -15 to -10°C.
resilience: Cold hardy and vigorous when established but performs best with shelter and adequate moisture.
uses: Sunny walls, fences, pergolas, trellis and ornamental foliage displays.
foliage: Deciduous; ovate green leaves on mature plants develop striking silver-white areas followed by pink flushing.
container: Possible while young in a large container with support, but ultimately much better suited to open ground.
uncertain: Plants are normally dioecious, with male and female flowers on separate plants. Sex was not specified on the supplied label; the strongest ornamental variegation is often associated with mature male plants.
